purpose: Defines the design method that turns requirements into design: viewpoints, inputs and deliverables, and Steps 0 to 6 from scenario reading through contracts and detailed design to consistency checks.
summary: Rationale: requirements decompose into information, actions and scenarios, rewritten as responsibility, behavior, contract and maturity viewpoints
Reasons for responsibility-named classes, class and sequence diagrams, actor selection, self-messages and contracts
Inputs (requirements, glossary, non-functional requirements, project rules) are not modified; issues return as questions
Deliverables table: scenario table, class definitions, class diagram, glossary, sequence diagrams, shared data, module table, detailed design, traceability table
Step 0-1: read inputs and read requirements as scenarios using EARS types
Step 2-3: find responsibilities as classes and act out scenarios in sequence diagrams
Step 4: write contracts via shared data definitions and module tables with preconditions, postconditions and failure behavior
Step 5: detailed design covering means, structures, libraries, algorithms and operating principles
Step 6: traceability table and consistency checklist before approval
Scope ends at design; implementation planning is out of scope
tasks: Creating a design document from requirements
Writing sequence diagrams and class diagrams
Writing a module table or shared data definition
Deciding actors and self-messages in diagrams
title: 設計手法
